title: Supported newborns take brisk steps when their feet touch a surface
summary: MedlinePlus says a supported newborn takes brisk steps when both feet are placed on a surface.
body: MedlinePlus describes a stepping reflex in the newborn to 2 month span. With the body supported and both feet placed on a surface, the infant takes brisk steps. The page gives that pattern a second label as well, but the body is held the whole time. This card is that supported pattern only. It is not the later skill of crossing a room with empty hands, and it is not a finding about one baby.

sources.title: Infant - newborn development
sources.author: MedlinePlus
sources.note: Primitive reflexes bullet: Stepping and walking, takes brisk steps when both feet are placed on a surface, with body supported.
